Learning Objectives
In this unit, you will learn to
1) Define point of view and get familiarized with different types of POV
2) Evaluate the functions of different types of POV and how they function in various rhetorical situations
3) Investigate the same issue from different perspectives
4) Understand why people think differently about the same issue
5) Use appropriate words and sentences in narrative writing

LOLITA
Vladimir Nabokov’s novel Lolita (1955) is told by Humbert Humbert, who calls young Dolores Haze “Lolita.” After becoming her stepfather, he takes her across America and sexually abuses her. His polished account often excuses his actions and leaves Dolores little room to speak for herself. As we read, we must ask what his version hides.Classroom synopsis · not a quotation from the novel.

The Perpetrator Perspective
‘Lolita’ starts with a confession of a pedophiliac affair, giving us a conscious moral reason to keep reading or watching. Lolita's legs are undeniably lascivious. From the first stunning appearance in the erotic classic, a close-up of her legs in the splashing water.
The exquisite legs and feet took up a lot of shots, and those innocent movements were always stirring Humbert‘s lust, sustaining all his desires and intentions for Lolita. From the perspective of the man, the 12-year-old Lolita is described as a “bad girl” who seduces men with a charming appearance.
Lolita, light of my life, fire of my loins. My sin,
my soul. Lo-lee-ta: the tip of the tongue taking a
trip of three steps down the palate to tap, at three,
on the teeth. Lo. Lee. Ta.
She was Lo, plain Lo, in the morning, standing
four feet ten in one sock. She was Lola in slacks.
She was Dolly at school. She was Dolores on the
dotted line.
But in my arms she was always Lolita.

What is POV?
Definition:
Point of view asks who tells a story and whose experience the reader follows. The narrator’s access to events and thoughts shapes what the reader can know and infer.
Point of view signifies the way, a story gets told— the mode established by an author by means of which the reader is presented with the characters, dialogue, actions, setting, and events which constitute the narrative in a work of fiction.

texts.text:
Definition
In first-person narration, the storyteller speaks as “I” or “we”.
That voice may be an author or a character within a story.

A first-person narrator tells what they see, learn, or hear from others.
Their account is shaped by memory, feeling, and judgment.
Readers should ask what the speaker might miss or misunderstand.

“I was glad of it: I never liked long walks, especially on chilly afternoons: dreadful to me was the coming home in the raw twilight, with nipped fingers and toes, and a heart saddened by the chidings of Bessie, the nurse, and humbled by the consciousness of my physical inferiority to Eliza, John, and Georgiana Reed.”
我很高兴：我从不喜欢长途跋涉，尤其是在寒冷的下午：对我来说，最可怕的是在茫茫暮色中回家，手指和脚趾都被冻伤了，护士贝西的唠叨让我的心很难过，而我的身体不如伊莱扎、约翰和乔治亚娜-里德，这让我很自卑。
CHARLOTTE BRONTE
Jane Eyre

First-Person POV
Marlow narrates his story in the first person, describing only what he witnessed and experienced, and providing his own commentary on the story (of Kurtz). Marlow explains to his listeners that he hates lies, but later Marlow not only lies to Kurtz’s fiancée but perpetuates the greater lie that colonizers are honourable figures.
"You know I hate, detest, and can't bear a lie, not because I am straighter
than the rest of us, but simply because it appalls me. There is a taint of
death, a flavour of mortality in lies-which is exactly what I hate and
detest in the world-what I want to forget."
HEART OF DARKNESS

The Tell-Tale Heart, published by Edgar Allan Poe in 1843 utilizes this storytelling tool: the narrator recounts committing a brutal murder, all the while proclaiming his own sanity.
True! — nervous — very, very dreadfully nervous I had been and am; but why will you say that I am mad? The disease had sharpened my senses — not destroyed — not dulled them. Above all was the sense of hearing acute. I heard all things in the heaven and in the earth. I heard many things in hell. How, then, am I mad? Hearken! and observe how healthily — how calmly I can tell you the whole story.没错！--紧张--非常非常可怕的紧张，我过去是，现在也是；但你为什么要说我疯了？疾病使我的感官变得敏锐--而不是破坏--而不是迟钝。最重要的是听觉变得敏锐了。我听到了天上地下的一切。在地狱里，我听到了许多事情。那么，我是怎么疯的呢？听着！看我能多么健康--多么平静地告诉你们整个故事。

Second-Person POV: YOU
Definition: It is perspective used in narrative. The narrator tells the story to another character using ‘you’ and the story is being told through the addressee’s point of view (p.84).This name has been given to a mode in which the story get told solely or at least primarily, as an address by the narrator to someone he calls by the second-person pronoun ‘YOU’, who is represented as experiencing that which is narrated (2014:304)

McInerney

IG HT
It's Six A.M. Do You Know
Where You Are?
ISSUE 86, WINTER 1982
You are not the kind of guy who would be at a place like this
at this time of the morning. But you are here, and you
cannot say that the terrain is entirely unfamiliar, although
the details are a little fuzzy. You are at a nightclub talking to
a girl with a shaved head. The club is either the Bimbo Box
or the Lizard Lounge, It might all come a little clearer if you
could slip into the bathroom and do a little more Bolivian
Marching Powder. There is a small voice inside of you
insisting that this epidemic lack of clarity is the result of too
much of that already, but you are not yet willing to listen to
that voice, the night has already turned on that
imperceptible pivot where two A.M. changes to six A.M.

Han Kang’s Human Acts
“看样子要下雨了。”你低声自语。要是真下起倾盆大雨该怎么办？你把眼睛微微睁开，让一线光透进来，望向省政府大楼前的银杏树。树枝间的风仿佛有了形状，悬在空中的雨滴似乎正屏住呼吸，等待落下。等你完全睁开眼睛，树木的轮廓暗淡、模糊起来。过不了多久你就得戴眼镜了。［原文此处省略一句］也许你的视力现在已经差到不能再差，最终仍能不用眼镜也看得清？
"Looks like rain," you mutter to yourself.
What’ll we do if it really chucks it down?
You open your eyes so that only a slender chink of light seeps in,
and peer at the gingko trees in front of the Provincial Office. As
though there, between those branches, the wind is about to take on
visible form. As though the raindrops suspended in the air, held
breath before the plunge, are on the cusp of trembling down, glit-
tering like jewels.
When you open your eyes properly, the trees' outlines dim and
blur. You're going to need glasses before long. […] Perhaps your
sight's as bad now as it's going to get, and you'll be able to get away
without glasses after all?
ANOVEL
HAN KANG

你在回家的路上死去。那是一场车祸。没什么特别值得注意的，然而却致命。你留下了妻子和两个孩子。这是一次无痛的死亡。急救人员尽力抢救，但无济于事。你的身体被摧残得如此彻底，实际上你反而更好，相信我。就在那时，你遇见了我。“我…我发生了什么？”你问道。“我在哪里？”“你死了，”我平淡地回答道。没有必要拐弯抹角。
The Egg
By: Andy Weir
You were on your way home when you died.
It was a car accident. Nothing particularly remarkable, but fatal nonetheless. You left
behind a wife and two children. It was a painless death. The EMTs tried their best to save
you, but to no avail. Your body was so utterly shattered you were better off, trust me.
And that's when you met me.
"What... what happened?" You asked. "Where am I?"
"You died," I said, matter-of-factly. No point in mincing words.
ANDY WEIR'S
The Egg

Omniscient point of view:
The narrator knows everything that needs to be known about the agents, actions, and events and has privileged access to the characters’ thoughts, feelings, and motives; also that the narrator is free to move at will in time and space, to shift from character to character, and to report (or conceal) their speech, doings, and states of consciousness (2014:301-2)/(p.87). The author is godlike, seeing and knowing all. The author tells the reader about the thought processes of each character without worrying about how the information is obtained. (p.7)

By-and-by, Tom took Becky's candle and blew it out. This economy meant so much!
Words were not needed. Becky understood, and her hope died again. She knew that Tom
had a whole candle and three or four pieces in his pockets-yet he must economize.
By-and-by, fatigue began to assert its claims; the children tried to pay attention, for it
was dreadful to think of sitting down when time was grown to be so precious, moving, in
some direction, in any direction, was at least progress and might bear fruit; but to sit down
was to invite death and shorten its pursuit.
At last Becky's frail limbs refused to carry her farther. She sat down. Tom rested with
her, and they talked of home, and the friends there, and the comfortable beds and, above
all, the light! Becky cried, and Tom tried to think of some way of comforting her, but all his
encouragements were grown threadbare with use, and sounded like sarcasms. Fatigue
bore so heavily upon Becky that she drowsed off to sleep. Tom was grateful. He sat looking
MARK TWAIN
The Adventures of
TOM
SAWYER

As for Elizabeth, her thoughts were at Pemberley this evening more than the last; and the evening, though as it passed it seemed long, was not long enough to determine her feelings towards one in that mansion; and she lay awake two whole hours endeavouring to make them out. pages.html:
Tolstoy’s War and Peace
她的工作要求她做一个热心肠的人。有时，即使心里不愿意，但为了不使认识她的人扫兴，她也会竭力做个热心人。安娜·舍勒经常现出微微的笑容，这同她姿色已衰的相貌并不相称。不过，她好像一个被宠坏的孩子，明知自己有招人讨厌的缺点，却不愿也不能加以克服，甚至认为无须克服。
LEO TOLSTOY
WAR AND
PEACE
To be an enthusiast had become her social vocation, and some-
times even when she did not feel like it, she became enthusiastic in
order not to disappoint the expectations of those who knew her.
The subdued smile which, though it did not suit her faded features,
always played around her lips, expressed as in a spoiled child, a
continual consciousness of her charming defect, which she neither
wished, nor could, nor considered it necessary to correct.

Precise Word Choice
“Succinct” is one of the most accurate words to describe Hemingway’s writing style.
Hemingway often uses concrete nouns, direct verbs and spare dialogue. In “The Killers” and “Hills Like White Elephants,” ordinary speech leaves readers to infer fear and conflict from what the characters do—and what they avoid saying.
